Dordrecht
dor'drekt
n. (oldest city of Holland, English Dort; host of the Synod of 1618 to 1619 and of the Statenbijbel decision)
From Middle Dutch Dordrecht, the ford on the Thure; English Dort.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Dordrecht was the oldest city in Holland and twice the place where the Dutch churches settled what they believed. A synod met there in 1578; and from November 1618 to May 1619 the great Synod of Dort sat in the city, with delegates from England, Scotland, Switzerland, the Palatinate, Hesse, Bremen, Emden and Geneva alongside the Dutch, examined the five articles of the Remonstrants, and set out the Canons on unconditional election, definite atonement, total depravity, effectual calling and perseverance. The same synod commissioned the Statenbijbel, the Dutch state Bible translated from the original tongues, which did for the Dutch language what Luther's did for German. The dictionary records the city as distinct from its synod, which has its own entry, because the doctrine decided there is the dictionary's own: “he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world” (Eph 1:4).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines election as the act of choosing or selecting one or more from others, predestination as the act of decreeing or foreordaining events, and a decree in theology as the predetermined purpose of God.

expand to see more

ELEC'TION, n. [L. electio.] The act of choosing; choice; the act of selecting one or more from others.

PREDESTINATION, n. The act of decreeing or foreordaining events.

DECREE, n. In theology, predetermined purpose of God; the purpose or determination of an immutable Being.

FOREKNOWLEDGE, n. Knowledge of a thing before it happens; prescience.

Key Scripture

Eph 1:4 — "According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love:"

Rom 9:16 — "So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy."

Joh 15:16 — "Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain: that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you."

2Th 2:13 — "But we are bound to give thanks alway to God for you, brethren beloved of the Lord, because God hath from the beginning chosen you to salvation through sanctification of the Spirit and belief of the truth:"

Modern Corruption

The oldest city of Holland, where the Synod of Dort sat from 1618 to 1619 and commissioned the Statenbijbel.

expand to see more

Arminianism is a live corruption and the most popular error in the English-speaking church. In its modern form it rarely argues the five articles; it simply assumes that God's choice follows the sinner's, that the atonement was made for all without securing any, and that grace once received may be finally lost. Dort examined those propositions against Scripture and rejected them, and the dictionary stands with the Canons.

The principle to recover is that election is God's eternal and unconditional choice, made in Christ, for His own good pleasure. The timing settles the question of ground: “According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world” (Eph 1:4). Human will and effort are both excluded as the cause: “So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy” (Rom 9:16). The Lord states the direction of the choosing: “Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you” (Joh 15:16). And the means are given with the end: “God hath from the beginning chosen you to salvation through sanctification of the Spirit and belief of the truth” (2Th 2:13).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek eklegomai (G1586), to choose out; Greek eleeo (G1653), to show mercy.

Greek eklegomai (G1586) — to pick out, to choose for oneself; Ephesians 1:4.

Greek katabole (G2602) — a founding, the foundation of the world; Ephesians 1:4.

Greek eleeo (G1653) — to have mercy, to show compassion; Romans 9:16.

Greek tithemi (G5087) — to appoint, to ordain to a purpose; John 15:16.

Greek haireomai (G138) — to choose, to take for oneself; 2 Thessalonians 2:13.

Usage

"“he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world” (Eph 1:4) — the Synod sitting from November 1618."

"“not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy” (Rom 9:16) — the five Remonstrant articles examined."

"“Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you” (Joh 15:16) — and the Statenbijbel commissioned."
